claim: The duplicate-key guard in the second member loop has its condition inverted. It reads `if (stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey))` where it should read `if (!stringMembers.ContainsKey(...))`. Because the dictionary starts empty, no string-keyed member from this loop is ever added. This loop sits after the property loop and is most likely the field loop. The generated formatter would then silently omit every string-keyed member it handles, so those values are never written or read. That is data loss, and it changes behaviour when SuppressSourceGeneration is unset or false, which the requirement forbids.
